_comment: Single source of truth for which languages this translator handles and
where the parallel text lives. Every script reads this file, so adding a
language is a config change plus a data file -- no code edits.
To add a language:
1. Add it to `languages` (code = what the HTTP API and your app send;
name = what appears in the prompt the model is trained on).
2. Add a corpus below naming its two columns.
3. Re-run prepare_data.py and retrain.
A corpus is either:
{ "file": "...", "columns": [A, B] }   one <sep>-delimited file, or
{ "dir":  "...", "columns": [A, B] }   an OPUS Moses folder (one
plain-text file per language).
`limit` samples a corpus down before anything else runs.
Pairs are emitted for every direction the data supports. A pair never
stated directly is still generated when both sides share one specific
translation in a third language, so bridging English in through Tagalog
yields English<->Cuyonon without translating Cuyonon twice.
ON THE REFERENCE CORPORA: the OPUS sets under corpora/ are downloaded, not
committed (see .gitignore) -- they are large and their licences vary. They
exist to make English<->Tagalog fluent. They are sampled hard on purpose:
the base model already knows English and Tagalog from pretraining, so it
needs far less data for that pair, while it has never seen Cuyonon. Left
uncapped, OpenSubtitles alone (1.07M pairs) makes Cuyonon 0.4% of the mix
and the model forgets it. Use --max-per-direction to set the final balance.
Re-download with the URLs in scripts/mine_english.py if corpora/ is empty;
every corpus below is optional and is skipped when missing.
corpora/hf-tagalog-english comes from the Hugging Face dataset
rhyliieee/tagalog-filipino-english-translation (Apache-2.0, 105k rows),
converted by scripts/import_csv_corpus.py. Read its register before
leaning on it: the rows are instruction-style prompts whose Tagalog side
appears machine-translated, so it is a good source of general fluency but
a poor match for this project's short conversational phrases. A third of
the original rows were dropped for exceeding the sequence length.
NOTE: serve.py validates `code` against this file, but your Supabase
`translations` table has its own CHECK constraint that currently allows
only 'tl' and 'cyo'. Widen it before sending a new code to production.
